rationale: Complaint about retyping dashboard figures into a warehouse implies a data-export capability that does not exist; no explicit ask, but the only remedy is a new feature.
Asks what an existing API's rate limits are; a request for information, not capability. Flips to yes only on the reading that the limits should be configurable.
Can you make the export include archived rows? Export exists but the requested behaviour does not; an enhancement phrased as a yes/no question.

Reports duplicated views losing column order and asks whether it is by design; framed as a bug but the author cannot tell bug from design. Honestly 50/50, labelled no because a question about intent is not a request.
The product behaves exactly as documented and the customer dislikes the documented behaviour; a design disagreement, not a feature request, though the fix would be a behaviour change.
How do I bulk-assign owners? is a support question whose honest answer requires the capability to exist, so it doubles as a request for it.
Asks where a shipped feature is in the UI; a discovery issue, not a request. Flips to yes if SSO in fact did not ship.
Feature exists for admins only and the customer asks for it for all users; "make X do Y" where X exists is an enhancement.
Frustration about support response times with no product ask; a service complaint. Some read "get back to me faster" as a request, but that is not a product capability.
Scheduling to email exists, but asking specifically for delivery into a Slack channel is a capability the product lacks.
A reproducible 500 with clear steps; a control bug that keeps the fixture from drifting all-ambiguous.
200 rows a week by hand with no named feature; an implicit automation request. Honestly 50/50 — some would dismiss it as vague feedback, but the workload points at a specific missing capability.
Asks for a discount at renewal; a commercial request, not a product feature.
Monthly report export exists as CSV and finance wants Excel; an enhancement to an existing feature.
Pre-sales question about whether the data model supports multi-currency; asks for an answer, not the capability. A salesperson might file it as a gap, which is the arguable part.
Bug report about a filter resetting that ends with an explicit "please make it remember" — an embedded feature ask inside a bug report.
Capability exists behind a setting the customer did not enable; a configuration/support issue. Arguable if the setting is undiscoverable, which would make it a UX request.
Notes a competitor capability and asks whether we plan to match it; competitive-parity request phrased as a question.
Calls the settings area confusing and asks for a redesign; subjective with no specific capability, but a redesign is a concrete change. Some would label it vague feedback — genuinely arguable.
Disputes a price increase; billing, not product. Flips if they ask for a specific billing capability such as itemised invoices.
We cannot go live until the export handles 100,000 rows frames an adoption blocker that is implicitly a request for larger exports.
Asks for a walkthrough for new analysts; a service request, not a product feature.
API rejects unknown parameters and the customer asks for them to be ignored; a bug report that is really a request for changed error behaviour. Honestly 50/50.
I know it's not on your roadmap, but... followed by a described capability; explicit dismissal plus a capability description is still a request.
